variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: AI evaluation drift is the gap that opens when an evaluation suite no longer measures the behavior users experience in production. The application can change, production traffic can change, or the evaluator itself can change.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: System behavior changed
pairs.detail: A model, prompt, retrieval snapshot, tool contract, safety policy, or routing rule changed the user-visible result.
pairs.explanation: A model, prompt, retrieval snapshot, tool contract, safety policy, or routing rule changed the user-visible result.

pairs.label: Evaluator changed
pairs.detail: A judge model, rubric, judge prompt, deterministic checker, or human-review policy changed how the same output is scored.
pairs.explanation: A judge model, rubric, judge prompt, deterministic checker, or human-review policy changed how the same output is scored.

pairs.label: Population changed
pairs.detail: The mix of languages, intents, tenants, risk classes, or request difficulty changed even when within-slice behavior stayed stable.
pairs.explanation: The mix of languages, intents, tenants, risk classes, or request difficulty changed even when within-slice behavior stayed stable.

pairs.label: Instrumentation changed
pairs.detail: Sampling, event definitions, missing joins, delayed labels, or duplicated records changed the evidence before scoring began.
pairs.explanation: Sampling, event definitions, missing joins, delayed labels, or duplicated records changed the evidence before scoring began.

variants.hint:
System behavior changed: A model, prompt, retrieval snapshot, tool contract, safety policy, or routing rule changed the user-visible result.

Evaluator changed: A judge model, rubric, judge prompt, deterministic checker, or human-review policy changed how the same output is scored.

Population changed: The mix of languages, intents, tenants, risk classes, or request difficulty changed even when within-slice behavior stayed stable.

Instrumentation changed: Sampling, event definitions, missing joins, delayed labels, or duplicated records changed the evidence before scoring began.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.label: Declare the change
pairs.detail: Record the candidate application and evaluator identities, affected claims, protected slices, and last known-good state.
pairs.explanation: Record the candidate application and evaluator identities, affected claims, protected slices, and last known-good state.

pairs.label: Run stable evidence
pairs.detail: Execute deterministic checks, frozen golden sets, hidden holdouts, paired judge anchors, and changed-path regressions.
pairs.explanation: Execute deterministic checks, frozen golden sets, hidden holdouts, paired judge anchors, and changed-path regressions.

pairs.label: Sample production
pairs.detail: Collect representative and risk-weighted traces with known selection rules, privacy controls, and delayed outcomes.
pairs.explanation: Collect representative and risk-weighted traces with known selection rules, privacy controls, and delayed outcomes.

pairs.label: Inspect slices and bounds
pairs.detail: Compare raw counts, uncertainty, disagreements, and critical cohorts before reading the aggregate.
pairs.explanation: Compare raw counts, uncertainty, disagreements, and critical cohorts before reading the aggregate.

pairs.label: Cap exposure
pairs.detail: Continue, pause, route around, or roll back with an owner, abort threshold, and tested recovery target.
pairs.explanation: Continue, pause, route around, or roll back with an owner, abort threshold, and tested recovery target.

pairs.label: Refresh without erasing history
pairs.detail: Promote confirmed production failures into a new regression-set version while preserving a hidden release holdout.
pairs.explanation: Promote confirmed production failures into a new regression-set version while preserving a hidden release holdout.

variants.prompt: What makes AI evaluation drift dangerous?
options: A familiar score can stop representing current production behavior.
Every evaluation run necessarily becomes slower over time.
A model must be retrained whenever traffic volume changes.
All production examples eventually become invalid JSON.
variants.explanation: System, population, evaluator, or instrumentation changes can break the meaning of a previously useful score.

variants.prompt: A critical language represents 3% of traffic. Why can a risk-weighted sample be preferable to a purely random sample?
options: It deliberately gathers enough cases to estimate the high-impact slice instead of letting volume determine coverage.
It makes confidence intervals unnecessary.
It turns the oversampled blend into the natural fleet average.
It guarantees every automated judgment is correct.
variants.explanation: Rare slices can receive too few random cases for a decision; risk-weighted allocation increases evidence where failure impact is high.

variants.prompt: The global score improves, but the lower confidence bound for a critical billing slice is below its release floor. What is the safe action?

Ship because the aggregate improved.
Delete the billing cases from the suite.
Lower the floor after seeing the result.

variants.prompt: Which comparison best isolates application behavior?

Compare two traffic weeks using different judges.
Average every slice into one score.
Ask only the current judge whether it agrees with itself.
